newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BORDEAUX CONTINUE QUEST FOR DOMESTIC CUP DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BORDEAUX CONTINUE QUEST FOR DOMESTIC CUP DOUBLE.

text.p: Bordeaux will be looking to win a battle between friends when they clash with Cannes in the French Cup third round on Saturday.
The League Cup finalists are favourites to brush aside Cannes despite being weakened by the absence through injury of French international Ibrahim Ba.
Triple French Cup winners Bordeaux are gunning for a place in the quarter-finals against a club with whom they have close links under coach Rolland Courbis.
Courbis is a close friend of Cannes administrative director Eric Goiran, with whom he worked at second division Toulon.

Since Courbis first took over at Bordeaux in 1992, 11 players have moved between Bordeaux and Cannes and this season Courbis reinforced his side with defender Jean Lambourde and midfielder Johan Micoud from the south coast club.
But the friendships stop at the touchline, Lambourde said.
"I've already met them (Cannes) in the (first division) championship. The emotional links are now cut. For me, it's a cup match with a qualifying place to be got," he said.
Bordeaux are on a roll, having followed up their League Cup semifinal win over Montpellier, which went to penalties, with a 4-0 home victory over Marseille in the first division last weekend.
They are unbeaten in eight matches in all competitions this year.
Their Ivory Coast international Cyril Domoraud, who was on African Nations' Cup duty last weekend, returns to the defence.
Francois Grenet will move up to an attacking midfield role to cover Ba's absence, while midfielder Didier Tholot could take the field as a striker alongside Jean-Pierre Papin.
Strasbourg, another in-form side who meet Bordeaux in the League Cup final in Paris on April 12, are away to third division Creteil.
Paris St Germain, who have won the French Cup twice since 1993, continue their run of visits to lowly opposition at fourth division Clermont.
The all-first division clash between Lille and Montpellier is on Sunday, while holders Auxerre, chasing a third French Cup in four seasons, were playing at second division Troyes on Friday night.
